label: Bible Study
prompt: Strength and honour are her _____; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
verse: Strength and honour are her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
note: From the virtuous woman poem — dressed in strength and honour, and laughing at the future.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and _____ unto me, and I will hearken unto you.
verse: Then shall ye call upon me, and ye shall go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.
note: From Jeremiah's letter to the exiles in Babylon: call on me, pray to me, and I will hearken.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with _____.
verse: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
note: Rehoboam ignored the elders' advice and threatened scorpions instead of whips — and the kingdom split in two.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself _____ from the world.
verse: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
note: James defines religion by orphans, widows and a clean coat — practice over performance.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God _____!
verse: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Israel: according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, What hath God wrought!
note: Hired to curse Israel, Balaam blessed instead: 'What hath God wrought!' — later the first message on Morse's telegraph line, 1844.
